_comment: SHARED cross-boundary contract for the dashboard WebSocket frame that the server
DashboardWebSocketHandler emits and the dashboard UI (store + panels) consumes.
This is the SINGLE source of truth pinning both sides to the same field names/types.
It is validated STRUCTURALLY, never by byte-equality of a captured golden:
- Java: DashboardWebSocketFrameContractTest drives the REAL handler, captures the
emitted frame, and asserts every field listed here is PRESENT with the right TYPE
(a SUBSET check - extra/optional/environment-dependent fields are ignored) and that
the server-assigned key correlations hold. It never asserts dynamic values,
timestamps, UUIDs or array ordering.
- UI: dashboardFrameContract.test.ts feeds `representativeFrame` through the real
store `applyMessage` and asserts the resulting store items expose exactly the fields
listed here (the same field names/types the panels read).
Because BOTH sides read `panels.*.requiredFields` from this one file, renaming or
removing a required field name here reddens BOTH tests - that is the cross-boundary
drift bite. A server-side field rename (without editing this file) reddens the Java
test alone (its required field is then missing from the real frame).
Determinism: because the Java check is a per-field SUBSET assertion rather than a
whole-frame equality, it is immune to non-deterministic emission ordering, UUID/
timestamp/port/hostname values, and environment-dependent extra fields - the exact
fragility that sank the previous byte-equal-golden attempt.

logMessages._comment: Log / Sessions panel. An item is a GROUP when it carries a `group` field (correlation-id roll-up), otherwise a plain entry. LogPanel discriminates with isLogGroup().

group._comment: LogGroup reads group.key, group.correlationId (shared by every grouped entry; the Explain action sends it), group.group (a nested entry) and group.value (the entry array).

activeExpectations._comment: Active Expectations panel. JsonListItem reads item.key and item.value (item.description optional).

recordedRequests._comment: Received Requests panel. JsonListItem reads item.key and item.value.

proxiedRequests._comment: Proxied Requests panel. JsonListItem reads item.key and item.value.

correlations._comment: A Received-Requests row's key is '<serverLogId>_request'; the same RECEIVED_REQUEST log entry appears in logMessages with key '<serverLogId>_log'. The shared server log id must tie the request row to its log entry - this proves the server key-assignment stays consistent across panels.

representativeFrame._comment: A representative, canonicalised frame with all four panels populated, mirroring the real DashboardWebSocketHandler output shape. Dynamic values are placeholders - only field names/types are contractual. The RECEIVED_REQUEST log entry (key 'srv-req-0001_log') and its recorded request (key 'srv-req-0001_request') share the server log id 'srv-req-0001' to satisfy the correlation above.
